record.paper_title: The formation and evolution of early-type galaxies : solid results and open questions
record.context_brief: Size evolution of compact high-redshift early-type galaxies
record.original_question: What explains the compact sizes of early-type galaxies at redshift z > 1, and how do these superdense galaxies increase their sizes enough to match the local Kormendy relation by redshift z approximately 0? The problem concerns early-type galaxies with effective radii Re ≤ 1 kpc, sizes about 2--3 times smaller than present-day early-type galaxies, stellar mass surface densities up to about 10 times local values, and stellar volume densities up to about 30 times local values; it also asks whether the apparent size differences could be affected by observational biases such as surface-brightness dimming and signal-to-noise effects.

evidence.quote: Another property which characterizes ETGs at z > 1 is their compact structure [28], with sizes (Re ≤ 1 kpc) much smaller than in present-day ETGs.

Several studies have confirmed this property and showed that Re is typically smaller by a factor of ≈ 2-3 than at z ≈ 0, implying that the stellar mass surface and volume internal densities are up to ≈ 10 and ≈ 30 times larger respectively

This is difficult to explain with simple passive luminosity evolution models and requires that these "superdense" ETGs should somehow increase their size in order to match the local Kormendy relation at z ≈ 0

It is unclear how to explain these size properties in the context of ETG evolution, and subtle observational biases (e.g. surface brightness dimming and S/N ratio effects) should not be completely excluded yet.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Observations of early-type galaxies (ETGs)—galaxies dominated by an old stellar population, with elliptical or lenticular morphology and little ongoing star formation—at redshift z > 1 indicate that a substantial fraction are "superdense": they have effective (half-light) radii R_e ≲ 1 kpc, a factor of about 2–3 smaller than ETGs of comparable stellar mass at z ≈ 0, with stellar mass surface densities up to about 10 times and stellar volume densities up to about 30 times those of present-day ETGs. Local ETGs obey the Kormendy relation, an observed linear correlation between mean surface brightness ⟨μ⟩_e within R_e and log R_e.

(a) Identify the physical mechanism(s) by which ETGs at z > 1 attain such compact sizes and high central densities at formation.

(b) Determine a quantitative evolutionary scenario by which these superdense ETGs increase R_e (and decrease their stellar density) by the required factor of 2–3 between z ≳ 1 and z ≈ 0, in such a way that they end up on the local Kormendy relation, while preserving the old stellar populations (i.e., without significant new star formation).

(c) Assess whether observational systematics—in particular cosmological surface-brightness dimming (which scales as (1+z)^{-4} for bolometric flux), limited signal-to-noise in the outer low-surface-brightness wings of the light profile, and PSF effects—could account, in whole or in part, for the apparent compactness, rather than the size difference being intrinsic.
artifact.status_search_result: The compactness of high-z ETGs has been confirmed by multiple subsequent studies, ruling out observational biases as the dominant cause. The leading explanation for subsequent size growth is dry minor mergers, supported by both simulations and observations (e.g., Naab et al. 2009; López-Sanjuan et al. 2012; Bernardi et al. 2013), with size growing roughly as the square of mass for minor mergers. However, debate continues over whether minor mergers alone provide enough growth, with alternative/complementary scenarios (puffing up via AGN/stellar mass loss, progenitor bias, selection effects) still discussed. The problem is therefore considered partially resolved rather than definitively settled.

status_evidence.title: Minor Mergers and the Size Evolution of Elliptical Galaxies (Naab et al. 2009)
status_evidence.snippet: Minor mergers can efficiently increase galaxy sizes; size grows ~ M^2 for minor mergers vs ~ M for major mergers.
status_evidence.claim: Minor mergers proposed as efficient mechanism for size growth of compact ETGs.

status_evidence.title: Dry minor mergers and size evolution of high-z compact massive early-type galaxies
status_evidence.snippet: Sequential minor dry mergers are the most efficient at promoting size growth and decreasing velocity dispersion of compact massive ETGs.
status_evidence.claim: Dry minor mergers remain the leading explanation but debate persists.

status_evidence.title: Dissecting the size evolution of elliptical galaxies since z~1: puffing up vs minor merging
status_evidence.snippet: Compares puffing-up and minor-merging scenarios for size evolution since z~1.
status_evidence.claim: Multiple competing scenarios are still being evaluated.
